description: Models and tools for water quality improvement is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by EPA Region 10 (Pacific Northwest); EPA Office of Water; Washington Department of Ecology. Computer models are used extensively for water quality management and Total Maximum Daily Load studies. Models are tools used to predict how a water body will respond to changes in the amount of pollution loading a river or stream receives. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, Water Quality. Assets: Water Infrastructure – Drinking Water, Water Infrastructure – General, Water Infrastructure – Wastewater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
